event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CDW’s 2021-02-26 Form 10-K portrays COVID-19 as a present-day, multi-faceted threat that is already eroding performance and may intensify.  The filing repeatedly confirms actual adverse effects—supply-chain bottlenecks, vendor product constraints, labour and facility disruptions, slower customer payments, and higher credit-loss reserves—while also warning of future demand contractions and budgetary pressures across key end-markets.  Although most disclosures remain qualitative, they are company-specific (e.g., inability to meet customer demand, temporary distribution-centre closures, heightened credit-loss provisioning) and describe concrete operational chokepoints.  Few numerical impacts are supplied, so the language stops short of a “quantified materiality” tier, but the narrative clearly links recent-to-current losses with additional downside scenarios.  Because the filing date is less than one year after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle allows high scores (up to 10).  Overall, the risk evidence is recent, direct, and ongoing, meriting mid-to-high severities across the extracted sentences; only modest downward adjustments are applied for generality or embedded mitigations.

evidence_list.snippet: The outbreak of the novel coronavirus ("COVID-19") pandemic has adversely impacted and could continue to adversely impact our business and results of operations and could also adversely impact our cash flows, financial condition and liquidity.

components.reason: States that COVID-19 has already caused adverse impacts (realised harm).
Expands impact to multiple financial dimensions (cash flows, liquidity, etc.).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct acknowledgement of existing and future financial harm across several metrics justifies a high severity score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: The global spread of COVID-19 continues to create significant macroeconomic uncertainty, volatility and disruption.

components.reason: Highlights ongoing macro-level disruption attributable to the pandemic.
Statement is broad and not company-specific.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: While recent and relevant, the sentence is generic and therefore scores a moderate 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Many governments and health authorities have implemented recommendations or mandates intended to slow the further spread of the disease, such as shelter-in-place orders, resulting in the temporary closure of schools and non-essential businesses, or social distancing measures, resulting in modified operations of various businesses including ours, and these measures may remain in place for a significant period of time.

components.reason: Identifies specific government actions that disrupt operations (closures, social distancing).
Explicitly states that CDW’s operations are modified and that restrictions may be prolonged.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete operational restrictions with explicit link to CDW, earning a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: We could experience disruptions, including as a result of resurgences of COVID-19, that prevent us from meeting the demands of our customers, such as product constraints from our vendor partners and wholesale distributors and other disruptions to our supply chain, disruptions in or restrictions on the ability of our coworkers to work effectively, temporary closures of our distribution facilities, modifications in the operation of facilities that remain open and disruptions of commercial delivery services.

components.reason: Details multiple supply-chain disruptions (product constraints, delivery issues).
Mentions labour and facility disruptions (coworker effectiveness, closures).
Directly ties disruptions to inability to meet customer demand.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive, company-specific operational risks justify a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact of COVID-19 and measures implemented to slow the spread have caused and could continue to cause delay in, or limit the ability of, our customers to make timely payments to us and could materially increase our costs.

components.reason: Identifies delayed customer payments (working-capital risk).
Notes potential for material cost increases.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific financial stressors—slower receivables and higher costs—warrant a solid score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic and even after it has subsided, we may experience adverse impacts to our business as a result of the pandemic’s global economic impact, including any recession, economic downturn or volatility, government spending cuts, tightening of credit markets or increased unemployment that has occurred or may occur in the future, which could cause our customers and potential customers to postpone or reduce spending on technology products or services or put downward pressure on prices.

components.reason: Links pandemic to macroeconomic deterioration (recession, credit tightening).
Explains direct demand-side impacts (reduced customer spending, pricing pressure).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows how macroeconomic fallout translates into customer demand risk, scoring 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic continues to impact our business, results of operations, cash flows, financial condition and liquidity will depend on future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted, including, but not limited to, the duration, the severity and further spread of the outbreak, future resurgences and reimplementation of closures, the availability, efficacy and acceptance of a vaccine, and actions taken to contain the virus, and the effectiveness of these actions and how quickly and to what extent normal economic and operating conditions can resume and be sustained.

components.reason: Emphasises high uncertainty and multiple uncontrollable variables affecting impact magnitude.
Very general, forward-looking disclaimer without company-specific metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds context on uncertainty but is generic; net score limited to 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Weak economic conditions generally, sustained uncertainty about global economic and political conditions, government spending cuts and the impact of new government policies (including the introduction of new or increased taxes), or a tightening of credit markets, including as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, could cause our customers and potential customers to postpone or reduce spending on technology products or services or put downward pressure on prices, which could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations or cash flows.

components.reason: Explicitly connects pandemic-driven economic weakness to reduced customer spending and margin compression.
Embedded within a broader list of macro factors (less specific).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies demand and pricing risks linked to COVID-19 but within a mixed macro list, yielding a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Manufacturing interruptions or delays, including as a result of the financial instability or bankruptcy of manufacturers, significant labor disputes such as strikes, natural disasters, political or social unrest, pandemics (such as the COVID-19 pandemic) or other public health crises, or other adverse occurrences affecting any of our suppliers' facilities, could disrupt our supply chain.

components.reason: Names pandemics—including COVID-19—as a direct cause of supply-chain disruption.
Presented alongside other generic events, diluting specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Supply-chain disruption tied to COVID-19 earns 4 despite being part of a multi-factor list.

evidence_list.snippet: Given the COVID-19 pandemic, Education customers have prioritized their budgets towards IT spending while Healthcare customer budgets have been pressured.

components.reason: Highlights divergent demand shifts across key customer verticals due to the pandemic.
Indicates sector-specific budget pressure (Healthcare) affecting sales mix.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows real-time changes in customer budget behaviour; moderate severity at 3.

evidence_list.snippet: As the duration and ongoing economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic remain uncertain, current and future budget priorities and funding levels for Government, Healthcare and Education customers may be adversely affected.

components.reason: Warns of potential future funding shortfalls across major public segments.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking budget risk for public customers is relevant but less detailed, scoring 2.
